heading.en: Why do polarised sunglasses cut glare?

hook.en: Look at a phone screen through polarised sunglasses and tilt your head. The screen goes dark at one angle. Light has a direction of vibration.

title.en: Explain polarisation as proof that light is transverse
Use Brewster's law for polarisation by reflection

say.en: Look at a phone screen through polarised sunglasses and tilt your head. The screen goes dark at one angle. Light has a direction of vibration. In this lesson: Explain polarisation as proof that light is transverse.
Apply Malus's law.
Use Brewster's law for polarisation by reflection.

body.en: In unpolarised light the electric field vibrates in all directions perpendicular to the ray. A polaroid passes only the component along its pass axis, so it halves the intensity of unpolarised light. If plane-polarised light of intensity $I_0$ falls on a polaroid whose axis makes angle $\theta$ with the vibration direction, $I = I_0\cos^2\theta$ (*Malus's* law).
body.kn: ಧ್ರುವೀಕರಿಸದ ಬೆಳಕಿನ ತೀವ್ರತೆ ಪೋಲರಾಯ್ಡ್‌ನಿಂದ ಅರ್ಧವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಮ್ಯಾಲಸ್ ನಿಯಮ: I = I₀cos²θ. ಧ್ರುವೀಕರಣ ಬೆಳಕು ಅಡ್ಡ ತರಂಗ ಎಂದು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: In unpolarised light the electric field vibrates in all directions perpendicular to the ray. A polaroid passes only the component along its pass axis, so it halves the intensity of unpolarised light. If plane-polarised light of intensity I 0 falls on a polaroid whose axis makes angle \theta with the vibration direction, I equals I 0\cos^2\theta (Malus's law). Unpolarised gives one polaroid: I 0 over 2.

narration.en: Let us follow light through two polaroids and then see polarisation by reflection.

say.en: In unpolarised light the electric field vibrates in all directions perpendicular to the ray.
A polaroid passes only one direction of vibration. The light comes out plane polarised with half the intensity.
A second polaroid at angle θ passes only the component along its axis, so the intensity falls as cos squared theta.
This is Malus's law. At θ = 60°, cos²θ = 1/4.
Reflected light is completely polarised when the reflected and refracted rays are at right angles. Then tan i_B = n; for glass, about 56°.

narration.en: Unpolarised light vibrates in all directions; a polaroid passes only the part along its axis, so half the intensity gets through. A second polaroid (the analyser) at angle θ passes I = I1 cos²θ: nothing when crossed at 90°. Slip a third polaroid between crossed ones and light gets through again!
narration.kn: ಪೋಲರಾಯ್ಡ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮ್ಯಾಲಸ್ ನಿಯಮ. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

body.en: Sunlight scattered by air molecules at 90° is polarised. Light reflected from a transparent surface is completely polarised when the reflected and refracted rays are at right angles; the angle of incidence is then the Brewster angle, with $\tan i_B = n$.
body.kn: ಚದುರಿದ ಸೂರ್ಯನ ಬೆಳಕು ಧ್ರುವೀಕೃತವಾಗಿರುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿತ ಮತ್ತು ವಕ್ರೀಭವಿತ ಕಿರಣಗಳು ಲಂಬವಾದಾಗ ಪ್ರತಿಫಲಿತ ಬೆಳಕು ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಧ್ರುವೀಕೃತ; tan i_B = n (ಬ್ರೂಸ್ಟರ್ ನಿಯಮ).

problem.en: Unpolarised light of intensity 32 W/m² passes through two polaroids with axes at 30°. Find the emerging intensity.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Unpolarised light of intensity 32 W/m² passes through two polaroids with axes at 30°. Find the emerging intensity.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Unpolarised light of intensity 32 watts per square metre passes through two polaroids with axes at 30 degrees. Find the emerging intensity.
After the first polaroid: 32 over 2 equals 16 watts per square metre.
Malus: 16 times cos squared 30 degrees equals 16 times 3 over 4.
I equals 12 watts per square metre.
So the answer is 12 watts per square metre.
